notes: These are not official journal brand palettes.
Prefer semantic consistency across all figures in one manuscript.
Always test grayscale and color-vision-deficiency readability before submission.

okabe_ito_categorical.best_for: General categorical groups, line plots, bar plots, scatter groups.

nature_muted_evidence.best_for: Nature-style multi-panel figures needing calm, low-saturation evidence colors.
nature_muted_evidence.source_inspiration: Muted journal figure styling plus colorblind-safe contrast.

science_high_contrast.best_for: Dense comparison plots where groups must separate clearly.
science_high_contrast.source_inspiration: High-contrast research figure styling with colorblind-aware blue/orange/teal anchors.

cell_mechanism.best_for: Biology, pathway, mechanism, cell-state, and schematic figures.
cell_mechanism.source_inspiration: Cell-style mechanism figures with warm highlight and cool structural colors.

clinical_neutral_accent.best_for: Clinical cohorts, demographic comparisons, survival plots, and restrained medical figures.
clinical_neutral_accent.source_inspiration: Medical journal style: neutral base with one or two strong accents.

earth_continuous.best_for: Continuous environmental, spatial, intensity, or model-output data.

cividis_accessible_continuous.best_for: Continuous data that must remain readable for color-vision-deficient readers.

blue_orange_diverging.best_for: Effect direction, residuals, enrichment/depletion, and signed change.
blue_orange_diverging.source_inspiration: Blue-orange diverging maps used as red-green alternatives.

grayscale_with_accent.best_for: Print-safe figures, methods diagrams, and figures where one finding needs emphasis.
grayscale_with_accent.source_inspiration: Print-first journal figures with one color accent.
